# icons


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

An app needs its icon in several formats: an `.icns` file for a macOS
bundle, an `.ico` file for Windows, and a small PNG favicon for the web
page in the window. This module makes all of them from one square image.
It needs Pillow, which the `icons` extra installs. Most callers only
need
[`icons_for`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/icons.html#icons_for),
at the end of the page.

An `.icns` file is built from a folder of PNG files with fixed names,
which macOS’s `iconutil` tool reads. `ICNS_SIZES` lists the ten names
and the pixel size of each. The `@2x` names are double-size copies for
Retina screens, so some sizes appear twice and there are seven distinct
sizes. `ICO_SIZES` are the sizes
[`ico`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/icons.html#ico) puts in a
Windows icon by default.

``` python
ICNS_SIZES[:4]
```

    ((16, 'icon_16x16'),
     (32, 'icon_16x16@2x'),
     (32, 'icon_32x32'),
     (64, 'icon_32x32@2x'))

[`_open`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/icons.html#_open) loads
the source image as RGBA and checks it. An app icon has to be square and
at least 512 pixels wide. macOS draws icons at up to 1024 pixels, and a
smaller source would be scaled up and look blurred, so it is refused
instead. Any format Pillow can read works; the example opens a JPEG.

``` python
_open(root/'logo.jpg').mode, _open(root/'logo.jpg').size
```

    ('RGBA', (1024, 1024))

These are the two errors you get for a source that is not square or is
too small. The examples work in a temporary folder, shown here as
`/proj`.

``` python
Image.new('RGBA', (800, 400)).save(root/'wide.png')
for p in ('wide.png', 'small.png'):
    try: _open(root/p)
    except ValueError as e: print(str(e).replace(str(root), '/proj'))
```

    /proj/wide.png is 800x400; an app icon has to be square
    /proj/small.png is 128px; macOS draws icons at 1024 and will upscale this

### iconset

``` python
def iconset(
    src, out
):
```

*The `.iconset` folder `iconutil` turns into an `.icns`. Returns the
folder.*

[`iconset`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/icons.html#iconset)
writes the ten PNG files into the folder `out` and returns it.
[`icns`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/icons.html#icns) builds
the `.icns` file `out` from them with `iconutil`, then deletes the PNG
folder unless `keep_iconset` is set. `iconutil` only exists on macOS, so
elsewhere
[`icns`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/icons.html#icns) raises a
`RuntimeError`, as the second example shows. The folder is deleted
either way.

``` python
out = iconset(logo, root/'Set.iconset')
sorted((Image.open(p).size[0], p.stem) for p in out.glob('*.png'))
```

    [(16, 'icon_16x16'),
     (32, 'icon_16x16@2x'),
     (32, 'icon_32x32'),
     (64, 'icon_32x32@2x'),
     (128, 'icon_128x128'),
     (256, 'icon_128x128@2x'),
     (256, 'icon_256x256'),
     (512, 'icon_256x256@2x'),
     (512, 'icon_512x512'),
     (1024, 'icon_512x512@2x')]

``` python
try: print(icns(logo, root/'Demo.icns').name)
except RuntimeError as e: print(e)
```

    an .icns is built by `iconutil`, which only macOS has

### ico

``` python
def ico(
    src, out, sizes:tuple=(16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 128, 256)
):
```

*A Windows `.ico` from one square image. Pillow writes every size into
the one file.*

[`ico`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/icons.html#ico) writes one
Windows `.ico` file that holds the image at each size in `sizes`. A size
above 256 pixels, the largest an `.ico` can hold, is left out, which is
why the second example asks for 512 and gets only 16 and 32.

``` python
with Image.open(ico(logo, root/'assets'/'Demo.ico')) as im: print(sorted(im.info['sizes']))
with Image.open(ico(logo, root/'small.ico', sizes=(16, 32, 512))) as im: print(sorted(im.info['sizes']))
```

    [(16, 16), (24, 24), (32, 32), (48, 48), (64, 64), (128, 128), (256, 256)]
    [(16, 16), (32, 32)]

### favicon

``` python
def favicon(
    src, out, size:int=64
):
```

*Write a PNG favicon for the web UI.*

[`favicon`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/icons.html#favicon)
writes a PNG `size` pixels wide, 64 by default, for the web page.
[`icons_for`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/icons.html#icons_for)
writes every icon a bundle needs into the folder `assets`:
`favicon.png`, `<name>.ico` and, on macOS, `<name>.icns`. It returns
their paths by kind. Run it when you set up a project or change the
logo, then point `App(icon=...)` at the result. The saved output came
from a machine that is not a Mac, so it has no
[`icns`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/icons.html#icns).

``` python
made = icons_for(logo, root/'assets', 'Demo')
{k: Path(v).name for k, v in made.items()}
```

    {'favicon': 'favicon.png', 'ico': 'Demo.ico'}
